CA01-01.claim: Five sentences to say to yourself instead of “I’m fine.”

CA01-02.term: “This is a hard day, not a hard life.”
CA01-02.definition: Shrink the frame. Most bad days feel permanent at 23:00 and ordinary by lunch.

CA01-03.term: “I don’t have to win this one.”
CA01-03.definition: Some arguments cost more to win than they’re worth.

CA01-04.definition: Your effort and your reply. Not their mood, not the outcome.

CA01-05.definition: Rest first, then judge the week.

CA01-06.definition: A feeling said out loud usually gets smaller.

CA01-07.line: Pick one. Say it before bed.
CA01-07.action: Save it. Send it to the friend who’s always “good”.

CA02-01.claim: A boundary keeps you safe. A wall keeps you alone.

rows: Leaving them on read for a week

CA02-03.quote: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
CA02-03.note: A boundary is about what’s in your power: what you’ll do. A wall tries to control what they can reach.

CA02-04.title: Say what you’ll do, not what they must do
CA02-04.body: “If you shout, I’ll leave the room” is a boundary. “Stop shouting” is a wish.

CA02-05.title: Keep the door visible
CA02-05.body: End with when you’ll be back. That’s the difference between space and distance.

CA02-06.line: Boundaries let people stay. Walls make them guess.
CA02-06.action: Send it to someone who’s been building walls.

CA03-02.quote: We’d been friends nine years. He asked how I was. I said fine, the way I always did. He nodded, then didn’t move. “No, really.”

CA03-03.quote: I laughed. He waited. The kettle clicked off and neither of us got up. I told him about the job, then the not sleeping, then my dad, which I hadn’t planned to.

CA03-04.quote: He didn’t fix anything. He made the tea twenty minutes late and said, “Thanks for telling me.” That was the whole thing. I still think about the kettle.

CA03-05.line: Ask twice. Then stay for the answer.
CA03-05.action: Send this to the friend who asked you twice.
CA03-05.cite: A composite story, not one real person · Moodius

CA04-01.claim: Why you feel behind, even when you’re not

CA04-02.definition: We judge ourselves by looking at others, especially when we’re unsure. The feed gives you everyone’s best day, every day.

CA04-04.title: Compare with one person: you, a year ago
CA04-04.body: What can you do now that you couldn’t then? Write three.

CA04-05.title: Mute, don’t judge
CA04-05.body: If one account leaves you worse every time, it’s not a lesson. Mute it.

CA04-06.line: You’re not behind. You’re comparing the wrong things.
CA04-06.action: Save it for the next 1am scroll.

CA05-01.claim: Myth: a real Stoic doesn’t cry.

CA05-02.definition: He tells Lucilius the eyes shouldn’t stay dry, and shouldn’t flood either. Grief is allowed. Being swept away by it is what he warns against.

CA05-03.definition: In English, “stoic” came to mean showing nothing. The philosophy was about judging well, not feeling less.

CA05-04.title: Let it out, then let it move
CA05-04.body: Cry. Then walk, eat, call someone. Feeling it and functioning aren’t opposites.

CA05-05.line: Stoicism was never about feeling less. It’s about not being ruled by it.
CA05-05.action: Send this to someone who thinks they have to hold it in.

lines: Who’s the friend you’ve only ever asked once?
Don’t name them. Just text them tonight.
